commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
Review UI layout polish, and tighter skill rules for grouping, why, lookFor, and size.

UI
- Why, What, and Look for names sit above their text, and that brief stays near 68 characters.
- Each source leads with its text. The kind and the name sit under it.
- The file header is one row: path on the left, hunk range, counts, and Viewed on the right.
- The path button is only as wide as the path. A click on the gap collapses the hunk. A click on the path opens the file.
- A one-file group has no file rail. Under 1099px a multi-file rail starts collapsed, and the rail is narrower.
- Hunk blocks are rounded, with a border and no shadow. The active file in a multi-file group keeps the primary border.
- The overview and the header count files left to read. A skipped binary is an info icon on the overview kicker, and the card names the path.
- Overview story boxes use a lighter tint.

Skill
- Document why is the problem or goal a source states, in that source's words. A sentence that only says what the change does stays in the summary.
- Each source item is checked against the code at head. A divergence, a ticket item a later comment overrides, and a required manual step are document lookFor bullets. Test plans, QA notes, and out-of-scope lists are not items.
- A lookFor bullet states what the code at head does and what the reader would observe.
- Group lookFor covers a hidden behavior change, an equality or identity change, a workaround, production code in a test or tooling change, a setup script that deletes or overwrites a developer file, an unmentioned behavior change, and a review fix the hunk does not make obvious.
- One group is one concern: the code, its unit tests, and the one-line call sites and re-exports that serve it. A new harness sits with the build or CI that runs it. A feature spec sits with its seed and helpers. A small change has one to three groups.
- dependsOn stays inside one part. Unasked work that could have been its own pull request is its own part. Work that only enables the asked story stays with that story. suggestedOrder puts a part a later story builds on first.
- A mechanical summary says what the reader can skip and why that is safe. An identical copy sits with its source, and the summary says the copy is identical.
- A new contract that later groups depend on is large, and that size stays when those groups merge.
- Pins npx comprehende@0.9.1.
